rules.description: Action targets must be exactly one cardinal cell away; target z relative to the actor is -2 through +3.

evidence.note: V183 source comment and V181 regression evidence.

limitations: Static executable evidence and restoration regressions do not prove all action dispatch timing.

rules.description: A bridge ordered on water validates action height at the future deck z+1 rather than the water z.

evidence.note: Bridge worker path.

limitations: Not every original bridge-building scene has been dynamically compared.

rules.description: A completed bridge at DF100 must reject bridge repair/build orders; damaged completed bridges remain repairable.

evidence.note: Native-derived workBridge repair path rejects missing<=0.

limitations: The HTML repair rule is statically matched; whole-game bridge behavior remains partially unverified dynamically.

rules.description: Fence orders must reject DF200 complete cores, orphan caps, blocked two-level construction space, and out-of-range construction height while preserving damaged/new valid cases.

evidence.note: Fence worker path.

limitations: Long-run V182 75x100 tick test did not complete; subsequent releases retain the focused regression.

rules.description: Action 10 receives a packed target containing x/y/z; execution must keep the normalized stored z instead of re-searching the x/y column.

evidence.note: The worker decodes x/y/z directly from its target pointer and indexes the map at that packed level.
Dispatcher passes the unit target record at +0x16 directly to Action 10.
Real stage contains same-column fence cores at z=3 and z=38 used for the regression scenario.

limitations: Confirmed from static target-pointer flow and M_032 regression; full original runtime timing remains to be compared dynamically.

rules.description: Continue-mode production-base planning may acquire another base target at soldier strength 1; the final build can consume that last strength point.

evidence.note: The 0x400 continue branch calls the base repeat-planning wrapper 0x43e8bb.
Base repeat wrapper calls 0x43eb4c with action 4 and performs no soldier-strength check.
Generic repeat planner does not read soldier strength (+0x4); action 4 also bypasses the sole extra 0x43fb9b validation case.
Base construction derives a minimum contribution of 1 and can consume the final strength point.

limitations: Confirmed from static original control flow plus browser regression; no direct Windows runtime capture is available.

rules.description: Continue-mode production-base planning may choose the next target below 100 resources; at the work cell, insufficient funds keep Action 4 active for a later retry instead of ending continue mode.

evidence.note: The base repeat wrapper calls generic planner 0x43eb4c without a treasury check.
The generic repeat planner selects and stores the next Action 4 target without reading faction treasury.
At the actual base work cell, 0x430640 attempts to spend 100; insufficient funds return worker code 1.
The treasury spender checks the active faction resource, deducts only when sufficient, and otherwise returns 0.
Base worker return 1 bypasses finish/retarget handling, leaving Action 4 active for a later pass.

limitations: Confirmed from static original control flow and browser regression; the original Windows executable is not dynamically captured.

rules.description: Continue-mode production-base destruction must exclude the acting faction's own base tile 29+f while retaining enemy base tiles 29..32.

evidence.note: Action 8 repeat wrapper clears the eligibility table, marks tiles 29..32, then clears bit 0 for tile 29+current faction before calling the generic repeat planner.
The generic repeat planner writes the selected target and action 8 into the current unit when a candidate remains eligible.

limitations: Confirmed from static original eligibility-table control flow plus browser regression; no paid external runtime is used.

rules.description: When Action 10 removes a zero-DF fence core, the dispatcher finishes or continues the work in that same processing pass rather than leaving Action 10 active for one extra pass.

evidence.note: Action 10 removes the core/cap at zero work/DF and returns 0.
Non-final staged damage returns 3; only the removal path takes the non-3 return.
Dispatcher bypasses completion only for return 3; any other return enters the finish handler immediately.
Finish handler resolves continue/wait/normal work state in that same processing pass.

limitations: Confirmed from static original return-code flow plus browser regression; no paid external runtime is used.

rules.description: Touch focus/marquee recovery adapts original mouse interaction for mobile browsers and is not evidence of original Windows input semantics.
limitations: Must remain distinguishable from Original mode controls.

rules.description: After the source-side distance flood, path bytes are reconstructed from the destination toward the source by probing cardinal direction bytes 0,2,4,6 and accepting only a strictly lower distance. Equal-length shortest routes therefore use destination-side west/north/east/south tie order rather than source-side first-predecessor order.

evidence.note: The native route flood stores distance values while expanding cardinal direction bytes 0,2,4,6 from the source.
Route reconstruction resets direction to 0, advances by 2 through 0,2,4,6, accepts only candidate distance < current best (JGE skips ties), and stores (direction+4)&7 as the forward path byte.
The same 0x4424e0 reconstruction routine is called from player/general movement and multiple AI route-planning paths.

limitations: V189 restores the cardinal tie/backtrack rule for the HTML walk graph. Native special vertical/elevator path bytes handled separately around 0x4425fd..0x4427f6 are not newly claimed by this rule.

rules.description: Original moving lift tile 124 preserves a hidden 120/121/122/123 under-tile; source-side distance flood enters vertical up/down states at lift endpoints, target-side reconstruction emits vertical path bytes, and the moving platform carries a rider while reversing at endpoints with the native pause.

evidence.note: Initial tile 120 allocates one of four lift records, preserves the hidden under-tile, and exposes moving platform tile 124.
Neighbor resolution reads the hidden under-tile for visible 124 and applies special 120/121 height semantics.
Source-side distance field has vertical up/down queue states entered from effective lift endpoints.
Target-side reconstruction resolves 124 through the hidden tile and stores 0xFE/0xFF vertical path bytes.
Four lift records move one z level per pass, transfer hidden under-tiles, reverse at 120/121, pause 0x1e passes, and carry riders.
Original map provides the real z=8..16 lift shaft used by the RED/GREEN Chromium regression.

limitations: Confirmed from static executable control flow plus deterministic Chromium regressions on original maps; no frame-by-frame capture of the original Windows process was performed.
